design_changes: Practitioner generation now starts from a target answer and builds a concrete actor/task/circumstances with one unknown, inspired by EUR-Lex fact patterns and adapted to UN actors and source types.
Relevant case details replace fixed anchor counts and short word limits. Country, mission, period and attribution must distinguish the intended situation.
Requests, proposals and attributed findings remain eligible without being promoted to binding obligations, adopted measures or established events.
Clearly hypothetical conditions may instantiate explicit source rules; fabricated historical claims, unstated converses, sanctions and consequences remain invalid.
Answers remain one complete contiguous target span, with faithful translation allowed when the requested language version is absent. Context can identify referents but cannot supply answer substance.
French, German, Spanish and Chinese generation prompts replace the old prompt-plus-overrides with equivalent versions of the English contract.
The practitioner quality verifier uses the same case contract and existing five score keys. Consequence measures practical usefulness, not legal force. Category diversity is not required.
The shared UN faithfulness prompt adds a narrowly scoped practitioner-case clarification so hypothetical case facts are not scored as invented source facts.

validation.limitation: Static review and integration tests establish compatibility, not generated-question quality or verifier accuracy.
